desc:
The string s consists of the characters 0 and 1. There are exactly 2k different binary strings (codes) of length k. Return true if every one of them occurs in s as a contiguous substring, and false otherwise.

s = "00110110", k = 2
codes 00, 01, 10, 11 all occur -> true

s = "00110110", k = 3
only 6 windows exist but 8 codes are needed -> false
constraints: s consists only of the characters '0' and '1'
hints: Collecting the length-k windows in a set and comparing the set size with 2<sup>k</sup> is a valid approach. Can you make each window O(1) instead of O(k)?
A window of k bits is just a k-bit integer. Moving to the next window means shifting left by one, adding the new bit, and masking off the bit that left.
Use a boolean array of size 2k indexed by that number. Stop with true as soon as all 2k values were marked. Also note that you need at least 2k + k - 1 characters, which allows an immediate false.
editorial: The window ending at position i is the integer h = ((h << 1) | bit) & (2k - 1). This rolling value costs O(1) per step and is a perfect hash: different windows give different integers. Keep a bit array of size 2k and a counter of how many distinct values were marked; the answer is true once the counter reaches 2k.

There are only n - k + 1 windows, so if that is less than 2k the answer is immediately false. With the given limits this also bounds the table: the table is only worth building when n ≥ 2k + k - 1, hence 2k is at most about 9,000. Time O(n), space O(2k).
